title: nixos/wakapi: streamline password salt & smtp password config
reason: Applicable: real wakapi module + wired test. Real diff genuinely REMOVES 4 options (passwordSalt, passwordSaltFile, smtpPassword, smtpPasswordFile) via mkRemovedOptionModule, replaced by a new environmentFiles option.
targets_toml: single target wakapi, cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,wakapi], watch=[passwordSalt] (the removed option).

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: IMPORTANT, DIFFERENT SHAPE than the rendering-gap cases: at base, passwordSalt gets a REAL WITNESSED PASS verdict (a real predicate `mkIf (cfg.passwordSalt != null) "WAKAPI_PASSWORD_SALT=..."`, real test evidence at nixos/tests/wakapi.nix line 25 setting a literal string value, witnessed=True) -- the first live PASS verdict encountered anywhere in S5-A so far. At head it correctly transitions to OptionNotFound (the option is genuinely gone). UNLIKE every prior *_not_found<->*_not_found rendering-gap instance, THIS transition DOES render: raw.json shows notable_total=1 with a real 'new_inconclusive' bucket entry (subject=passwordSalt, message='no mkOption declaration found for this watched option'), and summary.md's rendered output genuinely shows a 'NEW INCONCLUSIVE' section -- not all-zero this time. This clarifies the boundary of the rendering gap: transitions INTO or OUT OF a real witnessed PASS/finding DO get surfaced; it's specifically the *_not_found<->*_not_found transitions (neither side ever had a witness) that fall through the renderer's bucket system. Not counting this as notable_actionable_presentations myself since the surfaced item is an honest INCONCLUSIVE disclosure (correct, safe behavior per this project's own CLAUDE.md doctrine), not a finding or PASS claim requiring correctness adjudication -- flagging for the coordinator's own classification call, not presupposing it.
